ai.definition: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is a form of encryption that allows computation on encrypted data without decrypting it first. The result, once decrypted, is equivalent to if the operations had been performed on the plaintext.
ai.howItWorks: Data is encoded into lattice-based ciphertexts which support basic arithmetic operations like addition and multiplication. These operations can be chained together for more complex computations. Periodic 'bootstrapping' processes are used to keep noise levels in check, ensuring that long chains of operations remain valid without decryption.
ai.problemSolved: Enables secure cloud computing where data privacy is paramount, allowing computations on sensitive data hosted remotely without revealing the data itself.
ai.buildProcess: Involves complex mathematical algorithms and requires significant computational resources for both encryption and computation processes. Current implementations are highly specialized software solutions.
ai.costDrivers: High computational overhead, need for advanced cryptographic expertise, and potential energy consumption due to intensive operations.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to move from research to more practical applications as technology matures and optimizations continue.
ai.regulation: Currently not regulated but may face regulatory scrutiny in the future regarding data privacy and security standards.
ai.risks: High computational costs, potential for noise accumulation leading to decryption errors, and limited current implementation capabilities.
ai.profitability: Uncertain due to current stage of development and lack of widespread adoption. Potential for significant impact on cloud services and sensitive data processing industries if fully realized.
ai.futureDevelopment: Expected advancements in algorithm efficiency, hardware acceleration, and broader industry support could drive wider adoption.

glossary.def: A form of encryption that allows computations to be performed on encrypted data without decrypting it first.
A cryptographic technique based on the hardness of certain problems related to lattices, often used in FHE schemes.
A process within FHE that refreshes ciphertexts to reduce noise accumulation and enable long chains of computations without decryption.

subsystems.name: Lattice cryptosystem core
subsystems.role: provides the mathematical hardness that keeps ciphertexts secure while still allowing computation.

subsystems.name: Encoding and packing
subsystems.role: maps ordinary data into polynomials that the scheme can operate on.

subsystems.name: Homomorphic evaluator
subsystems.role: performs addition and multiplication directly on encrypted values.

subsystems.name: Bootstrapping module
subsystems.role: refreshes a noisy ciphertext so that long computations remain possible.

subsystems.name: Key management
subsystems.role: generates and distributes the keys needed to encrypt, evaluate and decrypt.

subsystems.name: Application compiler and runtime
subsystems.role: turns a program into a homomorphic circuit and selects practical parameters.

buildSteps.title: Choose a scheme family
buildSteps.detail: Pick a construction suited to the data: exact integers, approximate real numbers, or boolean circuits.

buildSteps.title: Select parameters
buildSteps.detail: Choose polynomial degree and noise distribution to meet a target security level and the depth of the intended computation.

buildSteps.title: Generate keys
buildSteps.detail: Create the secret key, public key and the evaluation and rotation keys that let a server compute without decrypting.

buildSteps.title: Encode and encrypt
buildSteps.detail: Pack the data into polynomials and encrypt them into ciphertexts under the public key.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate the circuit
buildSteps.detail: The server performs additions and multiplications on ciphertexts; additions are cheap, but multiplications grow the noise.

buildSteps.title: Control noise
buildSteps.detail: Relinearise after multiplications, rescale where the scheme allows, and bootstrap when the noise budget nears its limit.

buildSteps.title: Decrypt and decode
buildSteps.detail: The data owner decrypts the result with the secret key and converts the polynomial back into useful data.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into an application
buildSteps.detail: Wrap the encrypted computation in a service that handles key exchange, parameter negotiation and result delivery.

prerequisites.why: it supplies the hard problems that remain secure even when an adversary sees many encrypted computations.
it makes arbitrary-depth computation possible, but current implementations are far too slow for many workloads.
the number-theoretic transform and related methods make the large polynomial operations practical.
general-purpose CPUs and GPUs are inefficient for the huge integer and polynomial arithmetic that FHE requires.
without agreed security levels and interfaces, deployments are hard to audit and compare.

pathway.unlocks: privacy-preserving demonstrations in cloud analytics and machine learning.

pathway.milestone: standardised parameter sets and mature compiler toolchains
pathway.unlocks: portable, auditable applications that developers can build without deep cryptographic expertise.

pathway.milestone: hardware accelerators for polynomial arithmetic and bootstrapping
pathway.unlocks: encrypted computation fast enough for interactive services.

pathway.milestone: widespread encrypted cloud and machine-learning services
pathway.unlocks: users can outsource computation without revealing their data to the provider.
